executive_summary:
Maybank retains a resilient income base: Q2 profit improved and its interim dividend rose to 31 sen, while H1 profit declined approximately 0.9% and revenue weakened. This supports income research rather than an accelerating-growth claim; distributions require bank-specific capital and credit validation. Maintain observation; the evidence does not yet establish a directional new-position advantage.

Price remains below both major averages with negative MACD momentum and weak 20- and 60-bar returns. Above-average volume accompanies a close near the recent low, while RSI around 40 supplies no confirmed reversal. Maybank benefits from resilient domestic activity, but the rate evidence does not prove a net-interest-margin uplift. Regional FX exposure and credit repricing make a neutral macro signal appropriate. Small H1 earnings deterioration supports relative resilience, but the income thesis and the bearish capital objection both depend on unextracted bank metrics. Neither demonstrates an adequately valued income purchase or an observed credit impairment. Dividend growth is a distribution fact, not capital validation.
bull_case: Maybank shows a relatively stable earnings base, a modest Q2 profit increase and a higher interim dividend. Round two quantifies the H1 decline at approximately 0.9% and narrows the thesis to income resilience validated by bank-specific capital and credit evidence. Strongest disconfirming evidence to caution: Q2 profit improved and the interim dividend rose to 31 sen, while H1 profit declined only approximately 0.9%, supporting a substantial resilient income base.
bear_case: H1 earnings and revenue declined, while the dividend and vendor P/E do not independently prove a sustainable income opportunity. Round two accepts resilience but retains missing CET1, asset-quality and funding checks as central objections.
key_uncertainties: CET1, asset quality, credit costs, liquidity and funding spreads.
Recurring-income/distribution coverage and matched bank valuation.
CET1, asset quality, credit costs and funding spreads.
Matched bank valuation and recovery confirmation; unchanged OPR does not establish NIM improvement.
Vendor financial statements lack verified fiscal/availability timing; vendor forward P/E is an estimate, and a matched normalised fair-value model is unavailable.
catalysts_upcoming: Next comparable issuer disclosure, date unavailable here: A subsequent comparable half-year reports attributable profit growth above zero, maintains at least the observed 31 sen interim distribution, and documents compliance with applicable capital/liquidity requirements without worsening asset quality, resolving the core income gates.
Reassessment trigger rather than a forecast: A distribution cut below 31 sen or disclosed breach of applicable capital/liquidity requirements would invalidate the retained income-resilience scenario.
